title: Nonforfeiture Practice Note: Paid-Up Additions at a Whole Life Insurance Reduced Paid-Up Election
content:
Paid-up additions on an Ashgrove Whole Life Insurance policy are treated at a reduced paid-up election by their size and age.

## Practice

1. Where the paid-up additions face is at least **10% (0.1)** of the base face, the additions continue in force as paid-up additions alongside the reduced face, so their cash value stays out of the net cash value.
2. Where the additions face is below 10% of the base face and every addition on the policy ledger was bought within the last **60** calendar months, the additions are folded into the net cash value at the dividend cash that bought them, that is the total cash recorded on the paid-up addition purchase entries.
3. Otherwise they are folded into the net cash value at their cash value.

The base face is the face amount on the policy record; the additions face and cash value are those on the policy record. The last 60 calendar months end today: a purchase dated later than the same day of the month sixty months ago is inside, one dated on that day or earlier is outside.

## Size and age matrix

| Additions face against the base face | Every purchase inside the last 60 months | Treatment in the net cash value |
|---|---|---|
| 10% or more | Any | Left out; additions continue in force |
| Below 10% | Yes | Folded in at the dividend cash that bought them |
| Below 10% | No (at least one older purchase) | Folded in at their cash value |

## Cases (hypothetical base face 100000.00)

- Additions face 10000.00: exactly 10%, the additions continue and contribute nothing to the net cash value.
- Additions face 6000.00 from three purchases of the last four years, bought with 1100.00, 1200.00 and 1300.00 of dividend cash, cash value 3900.00: folded in at 3600.00.
- Additions face 6000.00 where one purchase is seven years old, cash value 3900.00: folded in at 3900.00.
